sn29.1:1.1: Thus begins a series of four Saṁyuttas on various nonhuman entities. The content of these chapters is minimal, their intent baffling.
sn29.1:1.2: The “dragon” (nāga_) is a powerful ([pli-tv-bu-vb-pc51:1.4]()), bejewelled ([pli-tv-bu-vb-ss6:1.3.2]()) serpentine ([sn1.37:7.4](), [cp20:1.2]()) entity with fiery breath ([sn3.1:8.2]()). They dwell underground ([mn23:2.39]()), or in the ocean ([ud5.5:17.1]()), or in the mountains ([sn46.1:1.2]() guarding treasure that they stole ([kp8:4.3]()). They may be man-eaters ([sn6.4:9.2]()) or protectors ([ud2.1:2.2]()), and occasionally had to be engaged in magic combat ([pli-tv-kd1:15.2.3]()), [pli-tv-bu-vb-pc51:1.4]()). They are color-changers ([sn3.1:8.1](), [cp13:3.1]()) and shape-shifters who can temporarily take human form, but revert when they sleep.
sn29.1:1.4: These four are defined at [mn12:32.1](); see note there for Vedic and Jain sources.
